parsed.reason: This is exactly the right move. Hale names the task being done ("Pulling up gymnastics for the fall"), gives the honest state of the search ("Still digging on that one"), and hands it off to the right channel ("I'll text you what I find") — which has no wall between the assistant and the parent's workflow. The parent can hang up and get a text when there's something real to act on. No filler, no "let me" or "one sec," no false closure with "is there anything else." Clean, brief, and it's a true sentence: the search is happening, and the parent will get the results. Contractions feel natural. The response avoids the trap of either saying "nothing found" (which stops the parent from looking) or padding with caveats. It's the honest ledger row spoken in real time.
